title: Tanzanian Pilipili Prawns
community: Zanzibar — hot and fast coastal prawn
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Tanzanian Kamba wa Pili Pili — large Indian Ocean prawns marinated in a pili pili-garlic-lemon paste and grilled over charcoal until charred and intensely flavoured. The spiciest prawn preparation on the coast — not for the faint-hearted.
longDesc: Pili pili prawns are the bold expression of Zanzibar's chilli tradition — the Indian Ocean's finest prawns coated in the island's hottest pili pili paste and grilled over charcoal. Simple, fast, and extraordinarily good.
ingredients: 500g large prawns — split down the back, deveined
steps: Mix pili pili, garlic, lemon, oil, and salt.
Coat split prawns thoroughly, including cut flesh.
Grill cut-side down over high coals 2—3 minutes.
Serve with extra lemon and cold drinks.
chefTips: Split prawns cook faster — 4—5 minutes total.
Very short marination — lemon acid breaks down prawn flesh quickly.
The flesh should be lightly charred.
cookingScience: See TZA066 for prawn cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: Indian Ocean prawns from local Zanzibari fishermen.
culturalNote: Pili pili prawns are the dish that challenges — ordered by those who know, approached cautiously by those who don't. At Zanzibar's beach restaurants, they separate the initiated from the curious.
